'''Johannes Maria Jozef''' '''"Hans"''' '''van Leeuwen''' (5 August 1932 – 3 December 2024) was a Dutch physicist.

==Life and career==
Van Leeuwen was born in [[Heerhugowaard]] on 5 August 1932.<ref name=lu/> In 1962 he obtained his doctorate at the [[University of Amsterdam]] under professor J. de Boer with a thesis titled: "Diagram techniques in statistical mechanics".<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.albumacademicum.uva.nl/cgi/b/bib/bib-idx?type=simple;lang=nl;c=ap;rgn1=entirerecord;q1=Leeuwen;x=0;y=0;cc=ap;view=reslist;sort=achternaam;fmt=long;page=reslist;size=1;start=84 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200727202942/http://www.albumacademicum.uva.nl/cgi/b/bib/bib-idx?type=simple&lang=nl&c=ap&rgn1=entirerecord&q1=Leeuwen&x=0&y=0&cc=ap&view=reslist&sort=achternaam&fmt=long&page=reslist&size=1&start=84 |title=J.M.J. van Leeuwen, 1932 - |language=Dutch |publisher=University of Amsterdam |date= |archive-date=27 July 2020}}</ref> In 1969 he became professor of physics at [[Delft University of Technology]].<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://web.science.uu.nl/natuurkundiggezelschap/2018-19/20181204-VanLeeuwen.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190501081947/https://web.science.uu.nl/natuurkundiggezelschap/2018-19/20181204-VanLeeuwen.htm |title=Dinsdag 4 december 2018 Prof. Dr. J.M.J. van Leeuwen (Leiden Institute of Physics, Leiden University) |language=Dutch |publisher=Natuurkundig Gezelschap te Utrecht |date= |archive-date=1 May 2019}}</ref> He moved to the [[Lorentz Institute]] for theoretical physics of [[Leiden University]] in 1986.<ref name=lu/>

Van Leeuwen was elected a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1985.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/4453 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200620153407/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/4453 |title=Hans van Leeuwen |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=20 June 2020}}</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1994 "''For contributions to statistical physics, in particular to the understanding of static and dynamic correlations in fluids, and to real space renormalization group theory''".<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=V&year=&unit_id=&institution= |title=APS Fellow Archive |publisher=American Physical Society |date= |access-date=4 August 2020}}</ref> In 1996 Van Leeuwen received the [[Onsager Medal]].

Van Leeuwen died on 3 December 2024, at the age of 92.<ref name=lu>{{cite web|url=https://hoogleraren.leidenuniv.nl/id/1550 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200212214639/https://hoogleraren.leidenuniv.nl/id/1550 |title=Johannes Maria Jozef van Leeuwen |language=Dutch |publisher=Leiden University |date= |archive-date=12 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=115282}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lorentz.leidenuniv.nl/research/vanleeuwen/vanleeuwen.html|title=J.M.J. van Leeuwen, 1932–2024}}</ref>
